title: trace-cost-allocation-and-tenant-chargeback-proposal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working proposal for attributing operational tracing and telemetry costs to tenants and internal teams. Goal is to produce a pragmatic, low-query-cost approach to (1) surface which customers drive trace & query costs, (2) enable chargeback estimates for billing/accounting, and (3) preserve operator debugging ability without excessive retention expense.

Context / motivation:
- Observability storage and query costs have grown ~3x in the last two quarters driven by heavier trace sampling and session replays for inference regressions.
- Finance and GTM have asked for a path to estimate per-tenant observability cost so Dedicated customers can be price-accurately quoted and internal product teams can understand telemetry ROI.
- We want to avoid a full-fidelity per-span billing model (too much cost and complexity). This doc sketches a hybrid model: compact metering + sampled trace retention.

High-level proposal (three-tier attribution model):
1) Lightweight metering events (always-ingested)
   - Emit per-request metering record downstream of the router proxy with fields: tenant_id, route, model_variant, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, batch_size, kv_cache_hit_ratio (approx), predicted_token_cost, timestamp, region.
   - Metering records are tiny JSON lines; retained long-term (90–365d depending on class). They enable cost estimates without keeping full traces.
2) Bucketed trace summaries (aggregates)
   - Periodic aggregation job (hourly) that produces: per-tenant token-count, span-duration-p50/p95/p99, kvcache-warmth-index, avg-batch-size, model-fanout-count.
   - Aggregates are cheap to store and sufficient for chargeback and KPI dashboards.
3) Sampled full traces for debugging
   - Adaptive sampling: keep 1–5% of traces uniformly per-tenant and bump sampling to 100% for detected anomalies (spike windows, SLO breaches, rollout events).
   - Full traces include rich context (span tree, kernel timings, gpu-util hints) but are short-lived (30–90d) except for tagged forensic windows.

Key telemetry fields to add to spans and metering records (metrics definitions):
- tenant_id: string (primary attribution key).
- request_id: unique request UUID across the request path.
- model_variant: string (e.g., rwd/v2-7b-qat).
- seq_len_in / seq_len_out: integers for token economics.
- batch_size: integer.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: float 0–1 measured at router (simple estimator: hits/attempts).
- predicted_token_cost: float (pre-computed estimate using model variant + seq lens + batch).
- span_cpu_ms / span_gpu_ms: number (approx compute time per span, derived from kernel timers).
- storage_bytes_for_trace: integer (approx serialized size).
- trace_storage_tier: one of [meter_event, aggregate, sampled_full].

Dashboard & reporting primitives (proposed widgets):
- Tenant cost rundown: time-series of estimated daily cost (USD), split by metering buckets: token compute, trace storage, query load.
- Hotspot map: matrix tenant x model_variant showing cost per 1k requests and trend arrows.
- Cost per token vs perceived latency: scatterplot to expose cost/latency tradeoffs per tenant.
- Sampled-trace link panel: show top anomalous tenants with links to available full traces and last-kept trace age.
- Cost forecast: rolling 30-day projection using recent metering and known committed capacity for Dedicated customers.

Queries / SQL snippets (pseudo) to compute estimated cost per tenant: 
- base token compute estimator:
  SELECT tenant_id, SUM(seq_len_out * model_price_per_token) as est_token_cost
  FROM metering_events WHERE timestamp between X and Y GROUP BY tenant_id;
- combined estimate with trace storage:
  SELECT m.tenant_id, SUM(m.predicted_token_cost) + SUM(a.storage_cost) as est_total
  FROM metering_events m JOIN allocate_storage_cost(a) ON m.tenant_id = a.tenant_id
  GROUP BY m.tenant_id;
(implementation note: storage_cost should be computed from daily aggregate of storage_bytes * tiered_rate)

Sampling strategy (operational heuristics):
- Default sampling: 2% uniform across tenants to maintain baseline debugging fidelity.
- Escalation rules: increase sampled fraction to 10–100% for any tenant experiencing:
  - p95 latency > SLA threshold, or
  - error rate delta > 3x baseline, or
  - rollout flag toggled in the last 24h.
- Decay: auto-reduce escalated sampling back to baseline after 48–72h without further anomalies.

Privacy & compliance considerations:
- PII/PHI redaction applied at ingest: redact request text fields before traces leave private runtime. Keep redaction logs for QA.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments we tag traces with retention_policy_override but honor customer-configured retention windows.
- Implement a tenant opt-out metadata flag for minimal metering-only mode (no trace retention beyond aggregates).

Operational playbook (rollout checklist):
- Phase 0 (lab): prototype metering in staging with 4 customers simulated; validate size/ingest cost.
- Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 10 low-risk production tenants with conservative retention (meter events + aggregates + 2% sampling).
- Phase 2 (scale): enable across hosted, keep sampling rate, and build chargeback dashboards for finance.
- Monitoring: create alert on daily ingest bytes for metering stream > 2x baseline and on gaps between aggregates and metering (indicates lost events).

Open questions / design tradeoffs (notes to discuss):
- Attribution granularity: per-tenant vs per-team (some customers have >1 product line). Need mapping table in billing.
- Pricing model: should we bill raw observability cost or a surcharge to cover engineering time?
- Metering reliability: what to do on transient router failures—do we buffer locally or attribute to region fallback?
- Query cost attribution: how to fairly apportion dashboard/query costs consumed by internal users?

Next steps / owners: 
- Telemetry infra: Diego will prototype the metering event schema and light-weight producer (P0, 2w).
- Cost model: Priya will work with finance to map storage + query + compute unit rates (P0, 1w).
- Dashboards: Sofia will wire the tenant rundown widget and hotspot map in the observability playground (P1, 3w).
- Product sync: Marcus to align pricing and Dedicated contract language (P1, 2w).

Notes to future readers:
- This is an intentionally pragmatic proposal — aim to minimize storage blowups while preserving operator signal. Keep feedback iterative; treat 30d retention thresholds as parameters, not laws.
